sections.h2: Where is the Durham County deed counter and when is it open?
sections.html:
Deeds are filed on the second floor of Durham County Administration Building II, 201 East Main Street, Durham, NC 27701. The counter keeps weekday hours from 8:30am until 4:45pm, except on holidays, and callers reach staff at 919-560-0480.

Census estimates place Durham County at 347,240 residents in mid 2025, living on 286.53 square miles of land. Many sellers never see the counter. A law firm or title agent submits the signed deed and gets it back stamped. What you control is the document itself, so it pays to know the office's rules before you sign.

sections.h2: What fees does Durham County print for filing a deed?
sections.html:
A regular deed runs $26.00 when it has 15 pages or fewer, and $4 more for each page beyond that. Mortgages sit on a separate line, and filing the release of one costs nothing.

Durham County recording charges, quoted from the county's fee schedule page
DocumentAmount
Deed or similar instrument (not a mortgage)$26.00 covers 15 pages; $4 for every extra page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 covers 35 pages; $4 for every extra page
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Paper that breaks the format rules$25.00 surcharge
Additional instrument inside one filing$10.00 apiece
Release of a mortgage (satisfaction)No fee
Certified copy of a recorded paper$5.00 for page one, $2 for each following page

Every county uses the same scale, which comes from G.S. 161-10, and the money is collected at the counter.

sections.h2: How is the Durham County deed transfer tax figured?
sections.html:
North Carolina taxes each $500 of price or value at $1, and a leftover slice under $500 counts as a full unit. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the seller settles it at the register's office before the deed goes on file.

The proceeds split down the middle. Durham County keeps one half for its general fund, and the other half goes to the state in monthly remittances. Your settlement statement will show the amount, so check it against the contract price.

  • Because the seller carries this cost, factor it into any offer comparison.
  • Paying off a deed of trust at closing adds no filing charge for the release.
  • The statute measures the tax on consideration or value, so the deed's stated price matters.

sections.h2: Can a Durham County deed be sent in over the internet?
sections.html:
Yes, through any of four vendors the county names. A deed that arrives before 4:45 pm is processed and sent back the same business day, and an individual who wants an account contacts a vendor directly.

  • Simplifile
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • ePN, the eRecording Partners Network
  • CSC, the Corporation Service Company

Title agents often hold accounts already, which lets a Durham closing finish in one day. A seller signing outside a closing can bring the original to the counter in person.

sections.h2: Which format rules must a printed Durham deed meet?
sections.html:
The county's Document Recording Standards page repeats the format rules from G.S. 161-14(b). A paper that misses one is still filed once the $25.00 surcharge is paid. Use white letter or legal paper, typed on a single side, with the document type named at the head of page one.

  • Three inches of blank space above the text on page one.
  • Half inch margins on all remaining edges.
  • Print at 9 points or bigger, with pen allowed for blanks and corrections.
  • Plat maps sized at 18 by 24.

When tiny print is the only flaw, the registrar can waive the surcharge if the page is legible.

sections.h2: Why does filing the deed protect a Durham County seller and buyer?
sections.html:
Filing settles who stands first. Per G.S. 47-18, a deed cannot beat a lien creditor or a buyer who gave value until it is registered where the land sits, and between rival papers the earlier registration time prevails.

Staff index what they receive and cannot repair a recorded paper. The standards page names misspelled names, defective legal descriptions and wrong parcel numbers as errors outside its power. An indexing slip is reported by email, and the office answers with an Administrative Notice linked to the original entry. Proofread first.

The county also runs a Recording Notification Service that emails citizens when a document is recorded in their name, a handy guard against property fraud on a vacant house.

sections.h2: Who collects Durham County property tax, and how does it touch a sale?
sections.html:
Property tax is a separate office. Durham County Tax Administration handles it from 201 East Main Street, 3rd Floor (919-560-0300), and the county's latest reappraisal of real property took effect January 1, 2025.

Each year's bill is mailed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and the county suggests passing a misdirected bill to the new owner. Ask the tax collector what is owed before closing so the settlement agent can clear it. Our Durham, NC property tax guide covers due dates and relief programs.

sections.h2: How can I search recorded Durham County documents before I sell?
sections.html:
The county runs an Online Public Records Search, described as a database of recorded real estate and business documents. Looking up your own parcel before listing shows the deeds, deeds of trust and releases in the chain, so you can confirm an old mortgage shows as released.

That check suits inherited houses and owners who paid off a loan years ago, and a satisfaction is free to file. A certified copy of any recorded paper costs $5.00 for the first page and $2 for each added page.

The office handles more than land records. Its own description lists assumed business names, corporate and partnership certificates, military records, notaries and oaths, plats and vital records such as birth, marriage and death certificates. The fee schedule prices a marriage license at $60.00 and a certified birth or death copy at $10.00.

sections.h2: How big is the Durham County housing market?
sections.html:
The Census QuickFacts page for Durham County hints at the volume behind the register's filings.

  • Housing stock of 164,222 units in the July 2025 estimate, with 141,847 households counted in the five year survey.
  • Homeownership rate of 55.5%, with owner-occupied homes valued at a median $389,400.
  • Typical rent of $1,508 and typical household income of $82,316.
  • 4,772 building permits during 2025.
  • Population growth of 6.9% since the April 2020 estimates base, and 1,133.7 people per square mile at the 2020 count.

Because the transfer tax follows the price, a higher median value means a bigger tax line on the closing statement. That is one more reason to compare any offer against your net proceeds line by line, and to ask the settlement agent for an itemized estimate before you commit to a closing date.

faqs.q: Who pays the Durham County excise tax at a sale?
faqs.a: The seller. State law has the transferor pay it to the register of deeds before the deed is filed, at $1 for each $500 of price or leftover fraction. Half stays with Durham County and half goes to the state.

faqs.q: Does Durham County charge to file a mortgage payoff?
faqs.a: No. The county fee schedule shows no fee for a satisfaction, so releasing a deed of trust at closing costs nothing at the register of deeds.

faqs.q: What if my deed is printed in tiny type?
faqs.a: The office can still file it. Missing a layout rule triggers a $25.00 nonstandard surcharge, though the registrar may skip it when the only flaw is print under 9 points and the page reads clearly.

faqs.q: Can a homeowner e-record a deed alone in Durham County?
faqs.a: Usually through a vendor. The county names Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, ePN and CSC, and each sets up its own account. A submission received by 4:45 pm comes back the same business day.

faqs.q: How do I correct a misspelled name on a Durham County deed?
faqs.a: The office cannot change it, since it records and indexes documents as presented. Ask the closing attorney how to correct the deed itself, and email the office only for an indexing error, which it answers with an Administrative Notice.
